The Powwow Drum is the traditional large drum of the North American Indian nations, originating in the late nineteenth century on the Great Plains. The body is a wooden cylinder, usually 60–90 cm across, and the head is covered with animal hide. Its timbre is powerful, thick and deep, with a raw, sacred quality; the low-frequency resonance stands out and it can produce a stirring bass. It is used mainly at powwow gatherings and other pan-Indian cultural events, where it stands for tribal unity and cultural identity. The way it is struck is flexible and varied, it can produce rich layers of timbre, and it carries far outdoors.
Powwow Drum起源於北美大平原印第安民族，特別是北達科他州、蒙大拿州與加: The Powwow Drum comes from the Indian nations of the North American Great Plains, especially North Dakota, Montana and the Canadian prairie provinces. The large drum was developed by Indian tribes in the late nineteenth century, combining traditional drumming with Western influence. The powwow itself grew out of the gathering traditions of Algonquian-speaking peoples in the Northeast and later became a pan-Indian cultural event.

坐或站，將鼓置於身前合適位置。將鼓穩定放置於地面或夾於雙腿之間。用手掌或鼓棒敲擊: Sit or stand, and set the drum in a comfortable position in front of you. Place the drum firmly on the ground or hold it between your legs. Strike the head at the centre or near the edge with the palm or a stick; different positions give different timbres. How hard you strike changes the volume. The sound is made by striking, so watch where you strike and how hard.
如今，Powwow Drum已成為北美印第安文化的重要標誌，在各類文化節慶、舞蹈: Today the Powwow Drum is a major marker of North American Indian culture, used widely at cultural festivals, dance competitions and educational events. It stands for the Indian nations' hold on tradition and their affirmation of cultural self-determination.
樂鼓鼓聲雄渾有力，音色厚重而深沉，帶有原始而神聖的質感。其低頻共鳴極為突出，能產: The drum's sound is powerful, its timbre thick and deep, with a raw and sacred quality. Its low-frequency resonance is very prominent and it can produce a stirring bass; the range sits mainly in the low-middle register and is rich in harmonics. As the head vibrates the sound has clear layers, an attacking strike followed by a long resonant tail. Compared with the timpani of the Western orchestra, the timbre is warmer and fuller; compared with the bass drum of a kit, its frequency range is wider and the resonance more ample. The wooden resonating chamber of the body strengthens the low frequencies, so the sound carries far outdoors. Changes in the way it is struck produce different timbres, which gives it a wide expressive range: it is the most affecting instrument in indigenous culture.

鼓身採用厚實的木材製成，通常選用松木、樺木等共鳴效果良好的木材。鼓面和鼓底覆蓋動: The body is made of solid wood, usually pine, birch or another wood with good resonance. The top and bottom heads are covered with animal hide such as deerskin or cowhide, specially treated for durability and tone. The edges of the hide are usually lashed down with leather thongs or cloth strips. The stand is wooden, and a metal frame can be fitted underneath so that the drum is easy to carry and can be fixed in place. The whole structure is plain and sturdy and stands up to long use and outdoor conditions.
